title: Break-Adjusted GARCH Versus Deep Learning: Multi-Horizon Volatility Forecasts for Kenyan Equity, Currency and Global Oil Markets
content: This study compares break-adjusted GARCH and deep-learning approaches to forecasting volatility in crude oil prices, USD/KES exchange rate and NSE 20 Share Index. Daily returns are examined for variance shifts using a modified ICSS procedure. Expanding-window, rolling-window and break-adjusted GARCH forecasts are evaluated alongside neural-network forecasts at 1-, 20-, 60- and 120-trading-day horizons using rolling-origin validation and multiple loss measures. Two significant variance breaks are identified for equities and six for forex; none is detected for commodities, despite conspicuous crisis-period volatility. For the equity series, the FIGARCH persistence parameter declines from 0.259 (p = .017) before break adjustment to 0.142 (p = .382) afterwards, indicating that structural change explains part of the apparent long memory. Forecast rankings vary across markets, horizons and loss measures. Break-adjusted GARCH and FIGARCH are competitive at the one-day horizon for equities and forex, respectively, whereas CNN–LSTM performs strongly at longer equity horizons and LSTM leads the reported longer-horizon USD/KES comparisons. Conventional GARCH variants remain competitive for Brent at longer horizons. By evaluating variance breaks, persistence and multi-horizon predictive accuracy within a common framework, the study shows why neither parameter stability nor the general superiority of deep learning should be assumed in forecasting volatility.
